headline: Glowing jellyfish lights sky as SpaceX delivers hope to space station
meta_description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket created a spectacular glowing jellyfish shape across the eastern US while delivering experiments to the ISS that could advance treatme…
summary_short: SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket painted the dawn sky with a glowing jellyfish shape on October 13, 2026, while carrying experiments to the ISS that could help restore vision an…
body:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket transformed the early morning sky into a breathtaking display of light on October 13, 2026, creating an enormous glowing shape resembling a jellyfish as it climbed toward orbit. The phenomenon, visible across the eastern United States, occurred when sunlight illuminated the rocket's expanding exhaust plumes high in the atmosphere just after the 6:33 a.m. EDT launch from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. But beyond the visual spectacle lay something far more significant: the Dragon spacecraft carried scientific experiments that could reshape medicine, including research aimed at restoring vision to people with certain forms of blindness and developing new treatments for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis.

This was SpaceX's 35th commercial resupply mission for NASA, and the cargo manifest reads like a roadmap to medical breakthroughs. Among the experiments aboard is one exploring the manufacturing of artificial retinas in microgravity—an environment where the near absence of gravity creates conditions impossible to replicate on Earth. Another investigation will use three-dimensional heart tissue models to revolutionize drug testing methods. Additional research will examine how new types of glass form in space and study brain organoids, tiny models of brain tissue grown from cells that could unlock targets for treating neurodegenerative conditions.

The mission also delivered the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, or IROSAs, scheduled for installation this fall to boost the orbiting laboratory's power supply. In that single launch, humanity achieved something remarkable: a moment of pure wonder in the sky paired with the quiet promise of medical advances that could touch millions of lives. The glowing jellyfish faded with the sunrise, but the work it carried upward continues.

Glowing jellyfish effect visible across eastern United States
Mission delivered artificial retina research and brain organoid experiments to ISS
SpaceX's 35th commercial resupply mission for NASA
Final solar array panels aboard to power the space station
